Business Delegate.why: Named Core J2EE pattern (Alur, Crupi, Malks); known mainly to enterprise Java developers, so a specialist tier fits.

Event Aggregator.why: Named enterprise pattern (Fowler's catalogue, also in Microsoft Prism); niche, so a specialist tier fits.

Chain of Responsibility.why: GoF pattern. The 'pattern' suffix alias is just the prompt's noun on the end, so it adds no entry. Widely known through middleware and servlet filters, so npe fits.

Servant.why: Named pattern from the Fowler/Johnson-era catalogue. I am not certain of the exact source, so this is a low-confidence keep; deep-internals tier is plausible.

Dependency Injection.why: Named pattern (Fowler's 2004 term, in Pico and Spring docs). Very widely known, so off-by-one is defensible.

Saga.why: Named distributed-transaction pattern from Garcia-Molina and Salem (1987) and the microservices literature. Systems and domain knowledge, so memory leak fits.

API Gateway.why: Named microservices pattern (Richardson, microservices.io). Systems and architecture people know it, so memory leak is a reasonable tier.

Dirty Flag.why: Named game-programming pattern (Game Programming Gems / Game Programming Patterns). Specialists know it, so race fits.

Bridge.why: GoF pattern, one of the best-known. Memory leak is too deep; it should be off-by-one or npe.

Execute Around.why: Named Smalltalk/Java idiom (Execute Around Method) that practitioners call by name. Specialist tier fits.

Data Transfer Object.why: Named pattern (Fowler, PoEAA). The DTO alias is an abbreviation of the kept entry and is fine. Many developers know it, so npe fits.

Composite View.why: Named J2EE presentation pattern (Core J2EE Patterns). Specialist tier fits.

Collecting Parameter.why: Named Smalltalk pattern (Beck, Smalltalk Best Practice Patterns) that practitioners use by name. Specialist tier fits.

Self Registration.why: I cannot place this as a named pattern in the GoF catalogue or a published pattern language. It reads as a descriptive phrase, so when unsure it is out.

Subclass Sandbox.why: I cannot confirm this as a named pattern in a published source. It is unsure, so it is out under the strict rule.

Table Inheritance.why: Not a named pattern. Fowler's catalogue has Single Table, Class Table and Concrete Table Inheritance; the bare phrase is a fragment of those.

Map-Reduce.why: A distributed programming model from Google's paper, not an object-oriented design solution or a GoF or pattern-language entry. Outside the accepts line.

Naked Objects.why: Named architectural pattern (Pawson and Matthews, Naked Objects). Niche but not internals-level, so heisenbug is too deep; race or memory leak fits better.

Page Object.why: Named test-automation pattern (Selenium community) that practitioners call by name. Many QA and test developers know it, so npe fits.

Resource Acquisition Is Initialization.why: Named C++ idiom and pattern (Stroustrup; POSA2 and Meyers-era literature) that C++ developers know well. npe fits.
